document.title: Memorandum of Mikhail Gorbachev's Conversation with Babrak Karmal, March 14, 1985
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: In his first conversation with Afghan leader Karmal, installed by Soviet troops in December 1979, Gorbachev stressed that Soviet troops cannot stay in Afghanistan forever and that the revolution was in its national-democratic stage. He urged Karmal to broaden the regime's base to unite all progressive forces and rely on his own forces.

events.description: Gorbachev meets Babrak Karmal in the Kremlin with Gromyko; urges broadening the PDPA base, says Soviet troops cannot stay forever, and Karmal pledges border defense.
Start of the 'new stage' of the revolution (Soviet intervention), when Karmal says most Afghans opposed the party and friendship with the USSR.
Gorbachev invites a DRA delegation to the 40th anniversary of victory in the Great Patriotic War.
Gorbachev meets Babrak Karmal in the Kremlin; Gromyko and Alexandrov present; Gorbachev stresses broadening the regime's base and that Soviet troops cannot stay forever.
Gorbachev elected CC CPSU General Secretary, congratulated by Karmal.

key_claims: Gorbachev told Karmal in March 1985 that Soviet troops cannot stay in Afghanistan forever.
Gorbachev urged the PDPA to broaden its social and class base and strengthen ties with the masses.
Karmal admitted the PDPA's weak connection with the people and that most Afghans opposed the party in December 1979.
Karmal identified strengthening the armed forces, working with tribes and defending the borders with Pakistan and Iran as key tasks.
Karmal framed the opposition as backed by American imperialists, Chinese hegemonists and Pakistani reactionaries.
Gorbachev stressed the main responsibility for defending the revolution rests with the Afghan leadership despite Soviet assistance.
